summary.text: 期 means a period, date, or time limit. Its 月-bearing form pairs a time-related meaning element with 其 as a sound element; early forms also contain 日, so the precise original motivation is unsettled.

formation.text: The 月-bearing graph is phonosemantic: 月 contributes a time-related meaning, and 其 supplies a sound cue. Shuowen glosses 期 as 會, “meeting,” and gives this analysis. Bronze forms are also reported with 日 and 其; a lunar-cycle explanation is possible, but is not established as the original motivation.

components.text: In the 月-bearing form, 月 contributes a time-related meaning. Bronze forms also use 日 in this role; the evidence does not settle the original motivation.
其 is identified as the sound element in 期. Though 其 itself is interpreted as an early picture of a winnowing basket, that picture does not contribute to this compound’s meaning.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied readings show the same Middle Chinese form, gi, and similar but distinct Old Chinese forms, *gə for 其 and *[g](r)ə for 期. This is compatible with a sound relationship, but the readings alone do not establish 其’s role in the graph; the modern pair is separate evidence and does not establish the ancient relation.

sound.text: The Baxter–Sagart 2014 table gives Middle Chinese gi for both 其 and 期.
The same table gives similar but distinct Old Chinese forms: *gə for 其 and *[g](r)ə for 期. This comparison is compatible with a sound relationship.
Modern Mandarin readings are 其 qí and 期 qī.

history.text: Bronze forms of 期 are reported with either 日 or 月 alongside 其. Shuowen calls 𣅆, written with 日 and 丌, an ancient form. Another study places the graph 期 in mid-to-late Spring-and-Autumn materials and treats 日-based spellings as earlier graphs for the word. These accounts do not settle the dating or sequence of the forms.

A bronze inscription uses the separate graph 其 to write the word 期. This is whole-graph borrowing: a written sign was reused for a different word because their spoken forms were similar. The basket’s ancient spoken name is not established, so it cannot independently explain the sound match.
朞 is documented as a variant of 期 with a rearranged graphic structure, not as a demonstrated ancestor. The evidence does not support a sequence 㫷 → 朞 → 期.

uncertainties.text: The precise dating of particular early forms and the priority of the attested meanings remain unsettled; the original motivation is not established as a lunar cycle.

senses.text: Shuowen glosses 期 as 會, “meeting”; this dictionary gloss does not establish it as the earliest meaning.

senses.period: Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscriptions; individual dating and priority unresolved
senses.text: A bronze inscription is interpreted as using 期 for a calendrical interval, though the example does not show that this use preceded other early meanings.

senses.period: Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscriptions; individual dating and priority unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples are reported for a limit or deadline. A modern study also cites transmitted poetry for appointed-time uses, though it identifies no dated manuscript witness.

senses.gloss: period of time, date, or time limit
senses.text: Current definitions include a period of time, a date, and a time limit.

limitations.text: The attested contexts do not establish a chronological semantic chain among meeting, calendrical interval, and limit or appointed time.
The evidence does not establish that present meanings developed from a lunar-cycle sense.

overview.text: 期 means a period, date, or time limit. It combines 月, a time-related meaning element, with 其 as a sound element; early forms leave the original motivation unsettled.

components.text: 月 contributes a time-related meaning in one reported form; the original motivation is unsettled.
其 supplies the sound element; the historical readings support a sound relationship, though they do not prove its role by themselves.
